answer:
Based on the World Spider Catalog data, here are the spiders of the family **Desidae** and genus **Desis** that are native to exactly one country/territory:

| Scientific Name | Location (Indigenous To) |
|-----------------|--------------------------|
| ***Desis bobmarleyi*** Baehr, Raven & Harms, 2017 | Australia (Queensland) |
| ***Desis galapagoensis*** Hirst, 1925 | Galápagos Islands (Ecuador) |
| ***Desis gardineri*** Pocock, 1904 | India (Laccadive Islands) |
| ***Desis inermis*** Gravely, 1927 | India |
| ***Desis japonica*** Yaginuma, 1956 | Japan |
| ***Desis jiaxiangi*** Lin, Li & Chen, 2020 | China |
| ***Desis kenyonae*** Pocock, 1902 | Australia (Victoria, Tasmania) |
| ***Desis risbeci*** Berland, 1931 | New Caledonia |
| ***Desis vorax*** L. Koch, 1872 | Samoa |

**Note:** The following *Desis* species are distributed across **multiple countries** and thus excluded:
- *Desis crosslandi*: Tanzania (Zanzibar), Madagascar, Comoros, Mayotte
- *Desis formidabilis*: Namibia, South Africa
- *Desis marina*: New Caledonia, New Zealand
- *Desis martensi*: Singapore, Indonesia (Java)
- *Desis maxillosa*: New Guinea, New Caledonia
- *Desis tangana*: East Africa (multiple countries)

**Desidae** is a family of spiders, some of which are known as **intertidal spiders**. The family is named for the genus _Desis_, members of which inhabit the intertidal zone. The family has been reevaluated in recent years and now includes inland genera and species as well, such as _Badumna_ and _Phryganoporus_. The vast majority of genera currently included in Desidae are native to Australia, New Zealand, or New Caledonia, although some are found in other parts of the world.
In 2017, the family Amphinectidae was merged into Desidae and the family Toxopidae was separated from it.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desidae#cite_note-wheeler-1) Those intertidal spiders that are truly marine commonly live in barnacle shells, which they seal up with silk; this allows them to maintain an air bubble during high tide. They emerge at night to feed on various small arthropods that live in the intertidal zone.
As now circumscribed, the family Desidae is mainly found in South America and Australasia, with some species reaching north to Malaysia.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desidae#cite_note-wsc-2)

_Metaltella simoni_ has been introduced in a large part of the Southern United States (records exist from California, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Florida). It is feared that it could extirpate the native titanoecid species _Titanoeca brunnea_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desidae#cite_note-edwards-3)

The spider genus Desis Walckenaer, 1837 is the type genus of the spider family Desidae Pocock, 1895. Desis spiders hide in silk sacs between rocks or shells during high tide and forage during low tide (Baehr et al. 2017). [Arachnida • 2020] Desis jiaxiangi • First Report of the Spider Genus Desis (Araneae, Desidae) from China, with Description of A New Species
Desis jiaxiangi Lin, Li & Chen, 2020
DOI: 10.11646/zootaxa.4755.3.11  
Photograph by Zixuan Lin.
The spider genus Desis Walckenaer, 1837 is the type genus of the spider family Desidae Pocock, 1895. Desis spiders hide in silk sacs between rocks or shells during high tide and forage during low tide (Baehr et al. 2017). Four Desis species have been recorded from Asia: Desis gardineri Pocock, 1904 (India), Desis inermis Gravely, 1927 (India), Desis japonica Yaginuma, 1956 (Japan) and Desis martensi L. Koch, 1872 (Malaysia) (World Spider Catalog 2020). Until now, only one species of the family Desidae, Badumna tangae Zhu, Zhang & Yang, 2006, has been reported from China (Zhu et al. 2006). Here, we describe a new species of Desis and report the genus from China for the first time.
Figure 4. Desis jiaxiangi, live holotype male.
Photograph by Zixuan Lin.
Desis jiaxiangi sp. nov.
Etymology. The species is named after Mr Jiaxiang Wu, the collector of the holotype; noun (name) in genitive case.

**Desidae** is a family of spiders, some of which are known as **intertidal spiders**. The family is named for the genus _Desis_, members of which inhabit the intertidal zone. The family has been reevaluated in recent years and now includes inland genera and species as well, such as _Badumna_ and _Phryganoporus_. The vast majority of genera currently included in Desidae are native to Australia, New Zealand, or New Caledonia, although some are found in other parts of the world.
In 2017, the family Amphinectidae was merged into Desidae and the family Toxopidae was separated from it.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desidae#cite_note-wheeler-1) Those intertidal spiders that are truly marine commonly live in barnacle shells, which they seal up with silk; this allows them to maintain an air bubble during high tide. They emerge at night to feed on various small arthropods that live in the intertidal zone.
As now circumscribed, the family Desidae is mainly found in South America and Australasia, with some species reaching north to Malaysia.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desidae#cite_note-wsc-2)
